newsitem.title: USA: Two officials under investigation leaving company.
newsitem.headline: Two officials under investigation leaving company.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co. said Thursday that one of two executives being investigated by the Justice Department in connection with a price-fixing scheme was retiring from the agricultural products giant and the other was taking a temporary leave.

The company said Michael Andreas, vice chairman and son of Chairman Dwayne Andreas, was taking a temporary leave of absence, and that Terrance Wilson, a vice president in charge of corn refining, has retired. ADM on Tuesday pleaded guilty to two counts of pricing-fixing and agreed to pay $100 million in fines to the federal government, the largest penalty ever in a criminal antritust case.

ADM, which advertises itself as "Supermarket to the World," has said previously that indictments were being considered against Wilson and Michael Andreas. It said Wilson was leaving for medical reasons.

ADM Chairman Dwayne Andreas apologised to shareholders Thursday for the "difficult situations" that the company faced over the past year. Like other ADM officials who spoke at the annual shareholders' meeting, he used mostly euphemisms to refer to the guilty pleas to two counts of pricing-fixing and the fines for fixing prices of lysine, a feed additive, and citric acid, used in foods, beverages and other products.
A proposal requiring the company's board be composed of a majority of independent directors was defeated, but received 42 percent of the votes cast.
